- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent high to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) mid-period, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract sentiment-driven downward bias.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns positive after a dip; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.
- In 30-day horizon, model often overweights early sentiment signals; reduce weight of first 5–7 days’ sentiment in averaging forecast weights.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), model tends to average or underreact; apply a 1–2% upward bias to compensate for sentiment inertia.
